To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) low-protein diets are effective in retarding the progression of renal disease, (ii) the mechanisms by which low-protein diets exert their beneficial effects are not well understood, (iii) the effects of low-protein diets on proteinuria and blood pressure are not well understood and (iv) the effects of dietary protein on renal disease progression are not the same in all forms of renal disease and may be different in men and women.
low-protein diets can slow progression of chronic renal disease in humans and experimental animals.
dietary protein restriction slows the rate of decline in renal function in patients with chronic renal insufficity and that the beneficial effects are independent of blood pressure reduction.

the mechanisms of protein-induced injury in chronic renal disease.
understanding the mechanisms by which protein restriction retards the development of renal failure.
the effects of dietary protein restriction on the progression of chronic glomerulonephritis and renal insufficiency, and with the mechanisms of action of dietary protein restriction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dietary protein restriction is a useful and safe adjunctive measure in the management of renal insufficiency and that it may retard progression to end-stage renal disease.

the evidence is strong for the use of low-protein diets in patients with end-stage renal disease, and that the evidence is suggestive for the use of such diets in patients with chronic renal failure, but not yet conclusive.
dietary protein restriction is beneficial to renal function, but only when renal function is compromised and only in the presence of adequate protein intake.

low-protein diets are safe and effective in slowing the progression of renal disease in humans, but the optimal composition and duration of the diet remain to be defined.
dietary protein restriction is an effective and safe therapy for the treatment of chronic renal failure.
